text:
Anaheim built a 2-0 lead on two Beckett Sennecke power-play goals, then watched Edmonton score five in the second period alone, four of them at even strength. Yet the box score tells one story and the chance quality another. ANA generated 3.2 expected goals to EDM's 2.69, attempted 74 shots to 43, and would have won 59 percent of simulated replays. The Oilers won by three goals because they cashed in far more than their chances warranted.

The second period was the exception. Edmonton had 1.29 expected goals to Anaheim's 0.39, and Evan Bouchard opened it eleven seconds in with a slap shot from Leon Draisaitl. Kasperi Kapanen tied it on the power play, Bouchard scored again, Vasily Podkolzin made it 4-2, and Connor McDavid finished it with a snap shot at 19:08. Draisaitl assisted on four of the goals. Bouchard's second goal carried a 5 percent chance of scoring, the sort of finish that rarely repeats.

Anaheim's trouble was in net more than in the shot count. Lukas Dostal allowed five goals on 2.15 expected, about 2.85 goals worse than average, before Ville Husso stopped both shots he saw. Devon Levi, meanwhile, stopped 29 of 31 and held the Ducks to two goals on 3.2 expected, a gain of 1.2 goals. Anaheim outplayed Edmonton across the night, but the one period that mattered went the other way.
